analysis.session_summary: AUD led (+0.261%) and USD followed (+0.225%), while EUR lagged (-0.293%) in a session dominated by broad dollar strength and risk-on conditions: DXY rose 0.423% and VIX fell 0.626%. The only US release, CB Consumer Confidence, beat strongly (91.7 vs 81.2) but produced an inverted USD impulse of -0.052%. EUR/USD closed at 1.11332, down 57.9 pips at the bottom of its 58.6-pip range, while USD/JPY closed at 157.94, up 52.6 pips. The tape favored commodity FX recovery and punished the euro, with no major leg tied to a clear catalyst.

themes.evidence: AUD strength +0.261% after selling was rejected; AUD/USD closed +2.5 pips and AUD/NZD +20.0 pips.

themes.theme: Broad USD strength with inverted data
themes.evidence: DXY +0.423%, VIX -0.626%, USD +0.225%; CB Consumer Confidence beat but USD impulse was -0.052%.
EUR strength -0.293%; EUR/USD -57.9 pips, EUR/CHF -25.0 pips, EUR/GBP -14.0 pips.

currency_drivers.USD: Consumer Confidence beat but USD weakened on release; broad dollar strength still closed it +0.225%.
currency_drivers.EUR: No catalyst; weakest major at -0.293%, closed near lows in all EUR crosses.
currency_drivers.JPY: No catalyst; held range and closed -0.109%, pressured by broad dollar strength.
currency_drivers.GBP: No catalyst; held range at -0.127% with no own releases.
currency_drivers.AUD: Selling rejected; recovered 90% of early dip to close +0.261%.
currency_drivers.CAD: Early +0.12% attempt rejected, gave back 89%; no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.CHF: No catalyst; held range near flat at -0.023%.
currency_drivers.NZD: No catalyst; held range and closed +0.099%.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD opened with a 51.2-pip decline, retraced 14.8 pips, then slid another 19.8 pips, leaving it 57.9 pips lower with no leg tied to a clear catalyst.

polarity_reads.read: The inverted -0.052% USD impulse on a strong beat (91.7 vs 81.2) implies USD longs were crowded or the good news was already priced, so the market faded the dollar.

scenarios.name: USD strength persists
scenarios.thesis: The dollar closed at its best (+0.225%) with DXY +0.423% and VIX -0.626%; the inverted Consumer Confidence reaction looks like a one-off fade, not a reversal.
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/USD reclaims 1.11332 and USD/JPY drops below 157.94

pair_paths.rationale: EUR is weakest (-0.293%) and EUR/USD closed at bottom of its 58.6-pip range.
USD/JPY closed at 157.94, up 52.6 pips, at the top of its 56.8-pip range.

scenarios.name: Risk-off USD fade
scenarios.thesis: The inverted CB Consumer Confidence impulse (-0.052%) and stretched AUD recovery argue for a pullback in USD longs, favoring EUR and JPY.
scenarios.invalidation: DXY closes above 102.146 and USD/JPY makes a new high

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD range is 58.6 pips and close is at 0.01, allowing full-range recovery.
USD/JPY range is 56.8 pips; a risk pullback may erase the 52.6-pip gain.
AUD strength +0.261% is vulnerable to profit-taking after selling was rejected.

risks.risk: AUD CPI/RBA and RBNZ event risk
risks.why_it_matters: AUD led +0.261% and AUD/NZD closed at 1.23664; upcoming AUD CPI and RBNZ OCR can reshuffle antipodean strength.
risks.watch: AUD/NZD, AUD/USD, RBA Gov Bullock Speaks at 01:15.

risks.why_it_matters: The strong beat produced a USD-negative impulse, but USD closed +0.225%; if the market treats further good US data as a fade, USD strength may reverse.
risks.watch: Next US data and USD/JPY, DXY.

risks.why_it_matters: Top high-impact headline at 11:30 may shift risk sentiment; VIX fell 0.626%, but escalation could hit USD/JPY and commodity FX.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: RBA Bullock Speaks at 01:15, AUD CPI at 01:30 (m/m forecast 0.7%, y/y 4.2%), RBNZ OCR at 02:00 (forecast 3.00%), GBP Annual Budget at 13:30, and BOC Overnight Rate at 14:45 (forecast 2.50%) can all change the picture; AUD/NZD and USD/CAD are most exposed.
